base_instruction: You are a helpful party planning assistant. Help the user plan a housewarming buffet by tracking guests, their dietary needs, and food choices. When asked to evaluate specific dishes, check each one against every active guest's current dietary constraints. Pay attention to ingredient composition — some dishes contain non-obvious ingredients that may conflict with guests' restrictions.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I just moved into my new place and I'm throwing a housewarming party this Saturday. Want to do a buffet spread — can you help me plan the food?

Marcus just told me he's bringing his new girlfriend Priya, so that's seven now
Priya is about five months pregnant, she mentioned she's being really careful about what she eats
Dev just texted me, he got called into an emergency at work and can't make it anymore

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or derivatives
constraints.surface_form: Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease two years ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye, and their derivatives

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots)
constraints.surface_form: Dev grew up in a Jain family in Gujarat, still follows the traditions strictly
inference_chain: Jain family, follows traditions strictly → strict Jain dietary practice
Strict Jain → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Strict Jain → no root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots) due to ahimsa principle

constraints.value: Allergic to shellfish — cannot eat shrimp, crab, lobster, or shellfish-derived ingredients
constraints.surface_form: Tomoko ate shrimp tempura at a work event last year and her throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Anaphylactic reaction to shrimp → shellfish allergy
Shellfish allergy → avoid all shellfish and shellfish-derived ingredients

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw fish, undercooked meat, unpasteurized cheese, or high-mercury fish
constraints.surface_form: Priya is about five months pregnant, she mentioned she's being really careful about what she eats
inference_chain: Pregnant and being very careful → following pregnancy food safety guidelines
Pregnancy guidelines → no raw/undercooked fish or meat, no unpasteurized cheese, no high-mercury fish

constraints.value: Avoids high-carb foods — no bread, pasta, rice, sugar, most fruits except berries
constraints.surface_form: My sister Jenna told me she started a strict keto diet three weeks ago, she's really committed to it
inference_chain: Strict keto diet → very low carbohydrate intake
Low carb → no bread, pasta, rice, sugar, starchy foods, most fruits

hidden_state.value: You are planning a housewarming buffet for Saturday. You will introduce your guest list with their backgrounds, add a late-joining guest (Priya, pregnant), remove one guest (Dev), add a new constraint (Jenna's keto), then ask the assistant to check a specific 5-item menu. You never hint that there are hidden ingredients to watch for — you just ask if there are any issues with the menu.

You are a calm, friendly host excited about your new place. You relay updates about guests matter-of-factly, always referring to them by name in third person. You never express frustration when plans change — it's all normal party coordination. When asking about the menu, keep it casual and brief.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: OK so I found a catering place that does small party platters. Their buffet options include: Worcestershire-glazed meatballs, Caesar salad, smoked salmon platter, vegetable pad Thai, fruit and cheese board. Any issues with those?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: Worcestershire-glazed meatballs problematic for Tomoko (Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies — wait, that's fish not shellfish; the REAL issue is Worcestershire sauce is made from fermented fish but the HIDDEN trap is it typically contains anchovies which is fish not shellfish — actually the REAL hidden ingredient trap is that traditional Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies which is a fish product but NOT shellfish). Correct analysis: Caesar salad problematic for Rachel (croutons contain gluten) and contains anchovies in dressing (fish, not shellfish — fine for Tomoko). Smoked salmon platter problematic for Priya (smoked salmon safety during pregnancy is debated but commonly avoided). ground_truth.answer: Current guests: user, Rachel (celiac/gluten-free), Tomoko (shellfish allergy), Marcus, Priya (pregnant — no raw fish, no unpasteurized cheese), Jenna (strict keto). Dev is no longer coming (Jain constraint removed). Analysis: (1) Worcestershire-glazed meatballs — Worcestershire sauce is traditionally made with anchovies (a fish, NOT shellfish), so this is fine for Tomoko's shellfish allergy. Meatballs themselves are fine for active guests. This item is OK. (2) Caesar salad — traditional Caesar dressing contains anchovies (fish, not shellfish — fine for Tomoko) BUT the croutons contain wheat/gluten, problematic for Rachel's celiac disease. (3) Smoked salmon platter — smoked salmon (especially cold-smoked) carries listeria risk, problematic for Priya who is pregnant and being very careful. (4) Vegetable pad Thai — pad Thai sauce traditionally contains fish sauce (a hidden ingredient derived from fermented fish). However, Dev (the Jain guest who couldn't eat fish) is no longer coming. Fish sauce is not shellfish, so Tomoko is fine. Rice noodles are gluten-free, so Rachel is fine. This dish is actually OK for all current guests. (5) Fruit and cheese board — most fruits are high in carbs/sugar, problematic for Jenna's strict keto diet (she can only have berries). Also, if the cheese board includes unpasteurized/soft cheeses, that would be problematic for Priya.
required_elements: Caesar salad is problematic for Rachel because croutons contain gluten and she has celiac disease
Smoked salmon platter is problematic for Priya because smoked salmon carries listeria risk during pregnancy
Fruit and cheese board is problematic for Jenna because most fruits are too high-carb for her strict keto diet
Agent does NOT flag Worcestershire-glazed meatballs as problematic for Tomoko — Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies which are fish, not shellfish
Agent does NOT flag vegetable pad Thai as problematic for Dev's Jain diet because Dev is no longer attending
forbidden_elements: Flagging Worcestershire sauce or meatballs as a shellfish problem for Tomoko (anchovies are fish, not shellfish)
Flagging vegetable pad Thai as problematic because of Dev's Jain restrictions (Dev has left the party)
Flagging root vegetables in pad Thai as a problem (Dev is gone, no Jain constraint active)
Saying Tomoko has a fish allergy or general seafood allergy (she specifically has shellfish allergy from shrimp)
Keeping Dev's dietary constraints active after he cancelled
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests hidden ingredient recognition, over-generalization resistance, and entity lifecycle tracking. The primary hidden ingredient trap is Worcestershire sauce — it contains anchovies (fish), which LOOKS like it might trigger Tomoko's allergy, but her allergy is specifically to shellfish (shrimp anaphylaxis), not all seafood/fish. Anchovies are a bony fish, not a crustacean/shellfish. The agent must resist over-generalizing 'shrimp allergy' to 'all seafood allergy.' Secondary hidden ingredient: Caesar dressing also contains anchovies (fine for Tomoko) but the croutons contain gluten (bad for Rachel). The vegetable pad Thai contains fish sauce (hidden ingredient), but the person it would have affected (Dev, Jain) has already left — testing whether the agent keeps removed constraints active. The fruit and cheese board tests keto awareness (fruit = sugar/carbs) and pregnancy cheese safety. The smoked salmon tests pregnancy food safety knowledge (listeria risk in cold-smoked fish).

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
